thread.title: Performance Of Dow Components In 2018 - SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (NYSEARCA:DIA)

author: Ploutos
title: Performance Of Dow Components In 2018 - SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (NYSEARCA:DIA)
text:
In 2018, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) featured some of the largest one-day sell-offs (in points terms in history) and the index's single largest one day point gain (December 26th). At the end of the year, after all this tumult, the Dow finished down 3.5%, its worst annual performance since 2008.
Below I have presented a chart of the performance of the constituents on the year. Fourteen companies posted positive returns and sixteen companies produced negative total returns.
The table below presents a more detailed look at performance with the 30 constituents in the index at the end of the year listed in descending order by their 2018 performance. Note that General Electric ( GE ), the third worst performer in the S&P 500 at -55%, is excluded here. The constituent was removed in late June in favor of Walgreens Boots Alliance ( WBA ).
Note that I have included the share price and index weight in this table. The Dow got its start in 1896 as a means for synthesizing the movements of industrial stocks into a single number. The index uses weights based on share price. Merck ( MRK ), which has nearly a $200B market cap, has 2.6 million shares outstanding. It could easily have 26 million shares outstanding, its price would be $7.64 instead of $76.41, and its weight in the index would have been 0.2% instead of 2.2%. Given that it was the best performer in the index, a lower weight would have lowered returns on the index. Merck would be worth the same, its capitalization would just be subdivided differently. It works in reverse as well, the relatively high weight to Goldman Sachs - the index's fifth largest constituent weighed on the Dow even though it is one of the three smallest companies in the index in terms of market capitalization.
While its adjusted price-weighting and narrow coverage universe are now archaic and anachronistic in the days of computerized calculations and alternative weightings, the DJIA has retained its status as a stock market bellwether for many Americans. It is notable that a cap-weighted version of the Dow components would have produced a positive return (+1.6% - the table above is weighted by end of year market caps). If the Dow produced a positive return, would that have changed your impression of the year?
The top 9 constituents in the Dow - Boeing ( BA ), UnitedHealthCare ( UNH ), 3M ( MMM ), McDonald's ( MCD ), Home Depot ( HD ), Goldman Sachs ( GS ), Apple ( AAPL ), Visa ( V ), and Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ) make up just under half of the Dow. If that does not look like your portfolio, then the Dow might not be the best performance gauge for your portfolio as exciting as those 1,000 point swings were in 2018.
